entries.title: Chromium picture on the GPU
items: Chromium profiles that play through the Edge picture now draw the page on the GPU. The browser window stays covered, and the key color is punched out of a capture sitting above the video.
The video window itself is unchanged, so PlayReady and Widevine stay where they were.
The page still reports itself as visible, so a covered window does not pause the app or stop it fetching segments.
The app waits for the first GPU frame before it loads the page. If that frame never comes, or the browser exits first, the session restarts on the older color-key path.
Clicks, the wheel, and keys on the picture go to the covered browser.
Requests to pluscdn.pl go through the emulator. That host rejects the page origin, so the local server fetches manifests and segments without one.

entries.title: Tizen 9, VIDAA 9, and Panasonic Fire TV
items: Samsung Tizen 9.0 (2025) is in the profile list. The page runs on Chrome 120 and the picture still goes through avplay.
Hisense VIDAA 9 (2025) runs on Chromium 111, with the picture on the Edge plane. VIDAA profiles also answer chipset, OS version, resolution, HDR, Chromium version, and menu language.
Panasonic 2025 is Fire TV, not my Home Screen. The page runs in Chrome 122, the picture goes through Edge, and Back is keyCode 4. A page recognizes the set from the AmazonWebAppPlatform user agent.

entries.title: Optional pace and memory cap
items: Moc telewizora, under the profile list, can slow the browser process toward the selected television and cap its memory.
The calculator asks for your core speed in GHz and suggests a percent of one logical thread that lands near the set. The thread count only translates that percent into a share of the whole processor.
Wpisz podpowiedź copies the suggestion into the field. You can type another percent, such as 20 or 60, or leave the field empty to leave the processor uncapped.
The memory field is a ceiling in MB for the whole browser process, not the JavaScript heap alone. Empty means no memory cap. The video plane stays outside both limits.
The numbers are saved on this PC, per television, in settings.json. The line under the profile list shows what the next launch will apply.

entries.title: PlayReady through Edge and a clean Chromium start
items: Profiles that play through the Edge picture now take PlayReady as well as Widevine. A page that only offers a PlayReady license, can start that stream.
Edge uses its software PlayReady decoder so the picture stays in the video hole. Hardware PlayReady would draw into a protected overlay the color key cannot show.
The page reports PlayReady variants as supported, so they stay in the catalog the same way Widevine variants already do.
Closing one stream and opening the next no longer stalls on a license or append error left over from the stream that just ended.

Chromium profiles sit on a black screen and load the app only after the window matches the TV size, or after a few seconds if it never does. Firefox and Electron open the page as soon as the window frame fits.
The yellow unsupported-flag bar, the translate prompt, password save, notification prompts, and the restore-after-crash banner stay off.

entries.title: Startup settings and Edge video for Titan and Panasonic
items: Ustawienia remembers a default app, a folder or an http(s) address, and fills it in at every start. Uncheck TV profiles you do not use and they leave the list; profiles added later stay visible until you hide them.
Titan OS and the 2016 Panasonic set play through the Edge picture under the page, because Chrome 122 and Firefox 44 have no Widevine CDM.
The Panasonic window hides the Firefox navigation bar, and hardware acceleration stays off so the video hole shows the Edge picture.
A clear stream starts without waiting for Widevine. A license request still opens the CDM, and the page reports Widevine variants as supported so they stay in the catalog.
The HbbTV profile is labeled WIP, and video/broadcast objects include fallback content so the broadcast picture stays visible.

entries.title: More TV profiles and a universal VOD sample
items: Profiles now cover Hisense VIDAA, Vizio SmartCast, Philips Saphi and Titan OS, HbbTV 1.5, Panasonic my Home Screen (Firefox 44), and Sony BRAVIA / Vewd, alongside the existing Tizen and webOS sets.
Each new profile pins its own engine and player path: Edge under the page for most Chromium sets, Chrome for Testing 122 playing in-page on Titan, and Firefox 44 for the 2016 Panasonic set.
samples/universal-vod is a remote VOD catalog that switches between AVPlay on Tizen and Shaka elsewhere, with clear, PlayReady, and Widevine DASH demos.

entries.title: Live debug preview
items: A phone-friendly preview on your LAN shows the console, network traffic, JavaScript memory, and the session log while the TV page is running.
The memory tab tracks the page heap and the video-plane heap separately, including a lighter object trace and optional full heap snapshots for spotting leaks.
The network tab lists requests as they happen, with filters and a look at headers and bodies.

entries.title: First public build
items: Windows app that opens a Smart TV page in a 16:9 picture and takes a remote (keyboard or gamepad) instead of the mouse.
Samsung Tizen profiles from 2017 through 2022, each on the Chromium version close to that year’s TV, with video through an avplay-style plane.
An LG webOS 4 profile whose page stays on old Chromium while Edge handles Widevine and decoding.
Sample pages for a Tizen key test, a Tizen video test, and a webOS hello page.
